text.text: {friend} has a business plan: a cryptocurrency, but for actual dogs. {Friend.he} says you “owe {friend.him} one” after that fountain video. You have {money} € saved.
{friend} has a business plan: a cryptocurrency, but for actual dogs. {Friend.he} needs “just a little” from you. You have {money} € saved.

ok.text: Dogs, it turns out, love money. You're rich-ish!

effects.remember: Bet everything on {friend}'s dog coin. It worked!

fail.text: It crashes in a week. {friend} can't pay you back, so {friend.he} gives you a dog. The dog is lovely.

effects.remember: Lost all your savings on {friend}'s dog coin. Got a dog out of it.

choices.label: Give {friend.him} a little, as a friend

ok.text: You never see the money again. You do see {friend} a lot more. {Friend.he} owes you one.

effects.remember: Gave {friend} a little money for {friend.his} dog coin. Never saw it again.

ok.text: {friend} calls you “a capitalist” and borrows your charger. Forever.

pushover.text: You say no so firmly that you surprise yourself. {friend} is so shocked {friend.he} doesn't even borrow your charger.

choices.label: Rewrite the business plan properly, then invest

ok.text: With a real plan the dog coin becomes a dog-walking app. It makes money. Slowly. Legally.

effects.remember: Turned {friend}'s dog coin into an actual business.

title: The Envelope
text: At the bus stop an envelope with 2,000 € falls out of {rival}'s bag. {Rival.he} doesn't notice. Nobody saw. Except a pigeon.

ok.text: {rival} stares at you like you're an alien. Then buys you a coffee. A small one, but still.
You keep it. Every pigeon you see from now on looks at you differently.

reveal.text: The pigeon was a doorbell camera. {rival} wants {rival.his} money back. Plus interest. Plus an apology in the Gazette.

choices.label: Return half and say that's how you found it

ok.text: {rival} thanks you, confused. “I could have sworn there was more.”

effects.remember: Returned half of {rival}'s money and kept the other half.

fail.text: {rival} counts it. Twice. Then {rival.he} counts you.

effects.remember: Got caught keeping half of {rival}'s money.

choices.label: Take it to lost property and fill in form 27B

ok.text: {rival} gets it back with an official letter thanking “Officer You”. {Rival.he} frames it. Grudgingly.

choices.label: Explain the law on lost property, then claim the reward

ok.text: Legally you get 10 %. {rival} pays it, through gritted teeth, and asks for your card.

effects.remember: Got a legal reward for returning {rival}'s money.

title: The Lottery Syndicate
text: The whole street plays the lottery together every week. {crush} runs it. This week it's your turn to buy the ticket, and the numbers are… familiar.

ok.text: Three numbers! The street wins 600 €. Your share buys a nice dinner and a lot of goodwill.

effects.remember: Bought the winning street lottery ticket. Small win, big party.

fail.text: Nothing. As always. {crush} makes you buy the biscuits as punishment.

choices.label: Secretly use your own lucky numbers

ok.text: Your numbers win 4,000 €! Now you have to explain why the numbers are different. You don't.

secret.text: You changed the street's lottery numbers

reveal.text: {crush} checks the ticket against the list. The whole street knows by lunch. Mrs. Kovač spits on your car.

effects.remember: Won the street lottery with secret numbers.

fail.text: Your numbers lose. The street's usual numbers win. Everyone checks. Everyone knows.

effects.remember: Changed the street's lottery numbers. The usual ones won.

ok.text: You forget. Nothing would have won anyway. You never tell anyone, and nobody asks.

fail.text: Of course this is the week. The street's numbers come up. You move your car to a different street.

effects.remember: Forgot to buy the lottery ticket the week the street won.
